newsitem.title: USA: Kohl shuns limos for tour bus at G7 summit.
newsitem.headline: Kohl shuns limos for tour bus at G7 summit.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton brought western informality to the Group of Seven summit here, but bulky German Chancellor Helmut Kohl contributed some populist style by travelling to and from sessions in a tour bus.
Kohl, who overshadows fellow world leaders at these annual meetings, regularly shuns the black Mercedes, Cadillac or Zil limousines his other partners prefer.
The chancellor now regularly uses a roomy bus on his travels abroad because of his size -- he stands 1.93 meters (six feet four inches) tall and tips the scales at around 115 kilos (250 lbs).

"It's a lot more comfortable," Kohl, 67, told ZDF television in an interview. "When I'm in a car, I'm cooped up -- that has something to do with my figure and my height, my head almost always bumps up against the ceiling."
Kohl, post-war Germany's longest-serving chancellor, admitted he also had his political image in mind.
"Wherever I go, I notice that people are astonished when they find out the Germans are travelling in a bus," he said. "They find that really relaxed, in a very friendly way."

Informality had its limits, though, even for someone as folksy as Kohl. He reacted almost in horror when Clinton suggested he and the other G7 leaders wear cowboy boots to the summit's gala dinner on Saturday evening.
